lesson.title: Niet/Geen Drill
lesson.subtitle: coffee, tea, time and water — choose the negator by what follows

hook.title: Choose by What Follows
hook.content: If the noun is indefinite, geen. If you are negating a verb, adjective or definite phrase, niet. The drink words make the choice visible.

pattern.title: The noun decides
pattern.content: Ik drink geen koffie: koffie is indefinite. Het water is niet koud: koud is an adjective, so niet. The negator sits before the thing it negates or at the end of the predicate.
pattern.trap_note: Geen is not a universal 'no'. It cannot negate an adjective or a verb on its own.

exercises.prompt: Match each English meaning with its Dutch twin (Niet/Geen Drill):
exercises.target_answer: niet, geen, de koffie, de thee, drinken, het water
exercises.meaning: not, no, none, coffee, tea, to drink, water
exercises.explanation: These are the anchors of "Niet/Geen Drill": read each Dutch form through the pattern, not as a new word.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence says: “I do not drink coffee.”?
exercises.explanation: “Ik drink geen koffie.” is the Dutch form; the other readings bend the pattern of “Niet/Geen Drill”.
“Ik drink thee.” puts the thought together the Dutch way — The noun decides.

diagnosis.slip: an English-shaped word order slipped in
diagnosis.cue: Geen is not a universal 'no'. It cannot negate an adjective or a verb on its own.

exercises.prompt: Which English sentence is built the Dutch way?
exercises.explanation: “Wij hebben geen tijd.” is word-for-word “We have no time.”. The odd English is the lesson — never a model to produce. Pattern: The noun decides.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
cues: It means: The water is not cold.
exercises.explanation: “Het water is niet koud.” reuses only material taught in “Niet/Geen Drill” — The noun decides.
exercises.affirmation: You heard “Het water is niet koud.” — a sentence built from the lesson's own Dutch, practising The noun decides.

twist.prompt: One more, no safety net — say: “I do not drink wine.”
twist.explanation: Wijn is indefinite, so geen; the verb drinken stays positive.

summary.outcome: Negate indefinite nouns with geen and adjectives/verbs with niet.
summary.takeaway: The negator is chosen by the thing being negated, not by the speaker's mood.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on De Brug: Word Order: The Dutch Bracket.

niet.etymology_derivation: The general negator; geen is its partner before indefinite nouns.

geen.etymology_derivation: The negative indefinite article: ne + een, the twin of English no.

koffie.etymology_derivation: The same loan chain as English coffee, through Dutch.

thee.etymology_derivation: The same Hokkien source as English tea, borrowed through Dutch.

drinken.etymology_derivation: English drink and Dutch drinken are the same verb.

water.etymology_derivation: English water and Dutch water are direct twins; German shifted t to ss in Wasser.
